29:1: Surah Al-Ankabut It is Meccan In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful As for the discussion of the disconnected letters, it was previously mentioned at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. And the saying of God the Almighty: Do people think that they will be left to say, “We believe and they will not be tested?” is a question of denial, and its meaning is that God the Almighty must test His believing servants according to their level of faith, as stated in the authentic hadith: “The people most severely tested are the prophets, then the righteous, then the next best and then the next best. A man is tested according to his religious commitment; if his religious commitment is firm, his trial will be increased.” This verse is similar to His saying: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while God has not yet made evident those among you who strive and made evident the steadfast? And a similar verse is in Surat Bara’ah. God says in al-Baqarah 2:“Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while such [trial] has not yet come to you as came to those who passed on before you? They were afflicted with poverty and hardship and were shaken until [even] the Messenger and those who believed with him said, ‘When is the help of God?’ Unquestionably, the help of God is near.” That is why He said here, And We have certainly tested those before them, and God will surely make evident those who are truthful and He will surely make evident the liars. That is, those who were truthful in their claim of faith from those who are lying in their words and claims. God, the Exalted, knows what was and what will be, and what would not have been, if it had been. This is agreed upon by the Imams of the Sunnah and the Community, and Ibn Abbas and others say this regarding His statement, Except that We may know, “Except that We may see.” This is because seeing is related to what exists, and knowledge is more general than seeing, as it is related to what does not exist and what exists. And the Almighty said: Or do those who do evil deeds think that they can outstrip Us? Evil is that which they judge. That is, let not those who have not entered into faith think that they will escape this trial and test, for what lies ahead of them is a punishment and chastisement that is more severe and terrible than this. For this reason, He said: Or do those who do evil deeds think that they can outstrip Us? That is, that they will escape from Us. Evil is that which they judge. That is, evil is what they think.

29:5: God the Almighty says: Whoever hopes for the meeting with God meaning in the Hereafter, and does righteous deeds and hopes for the great reward with God, then God will fulfill his hope and fully repay his deeds, for that will inevitably happen because He hears supplications and sees all that is. That is why God the Almighty said: Whoever hopes for the meeting with God - then indeed, the term set by God will come, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing. And His saying: And whoever strives only strives for himself is like His saying: Whoever does righteousness - it is for himself meaning whoever does righteousness - then the benefit of his work returns to himself, for God the Almighty is independent of the actions of His servants, and if they were all as pious as the most pious heart of any man among them, that would not increase His kingdom at all. That is why God the Almighty said: "And whoever strives only strives for himself. Indeed, God is free from need of the worlds." Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: A man strives even though he has never struck a day with a sword. Then the Almighty informed us that, despite His being independent of all creation, and despite His kindness and benevolence towards them, He will reward those who believe and do righteous deeds with the best reward, which is that He will forgive them the worst of what they did and reward them with the best of what they used to do. He will accept a small amount of good deeds and reward one for it ten times as much as it, up to seven hundred times, and He will reward the bad deeds with the same or pardon and forgive, as the Almighty said: “Indeed, God does not wrong by the weight of an atom. But if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.” And He said here: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely remove from them their misdeeds and will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do.

29:8: God Almighty says, commanding His servants to be kind to their parents after urging them to adhere to His Oneness, for the parents are the reason for the existence of man, and they are the ultimate in being kind to him, the father by spending and the mother by showing compassion. For this reason God Almighty said: “And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and to parents, good treatment. Whether one or both of them attain old age [while] with you, say not to them a word of contempt, nor repel them but address them with honorable words. And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy and say, “My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small.” And with this commandment of compassion, mercy, and kindness to them in return for their previous kindness, He said: But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. That is, if they are eager for you to follow them in their religion if they are polytheists, then beware of them, do not obey them in that, for your return is to Me on the Day of Resurrection, and I will reward you for your kindness to them and your patience in your religion, and I will gather you with The righteous are not in the company of your parents, even if you are the closest person to them in this world. A person will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection with those he loves, i.e., with religious love. That is why God Almighty said: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely admit them among the righteous. Al-Tirmidhi said in his interpretation of this verse: Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja`far narrated to us, Shu`bah narrated to us on the authority of Samak ibn Harb who said: I heard Mus`ab ibn Sa`d narrating on the authority of his father Sa`d who said: It was revealed about four verses. Then he mentioned his story and said: Umm Sa`d said: Has not God commanded you to be dutiful? By God, I will neither eat food nor drink until I die or you disbelieve. He said: Whenever they wanted to feed her, they would turn their faces away from her. Then this verse was revealed: And We have enjoined upon man, to be dutiful to his parents, but if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them (al-Baqarah 2:17). This hadith was also narrated by Imam Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan sahih.

29:10: God the Almighty says, informing us about the characteristics of a group of deniers who claim to believe with their tongues, but whose faith is not firmly established in their hearts, that if a trial or a trial comes to them in this world, they believe that this is from God’s punishment upon them, so they turn away from Islam. For this reason, God the Almighty says: And of mankind is he who says, ‘We believe in God,’ but when he is harmed for the sake of God, he considers the trial of mankind to be like the punishment of God. Ibn Abbas said: He means that his trial is that he turns away from his religion if he is harmed for the sake of God. Other scholars of the Salaf said the same. This verse is like the statement of God the Almighty: “And of mankind is he who worships God on the edge. If good befalls him, he is content therewith; but if a trial befalls him, he turns back on his face. He loses this world and the Hereafter. That is what is the manifest loss. * He invokes besides God that which does not harm him and that which does not benefit him. That is what is far astray.” Then God the Almighty says: If victory comes from your Lord, he will surely say, ‘Indeed, we were with you.’ That is, if a close victory comes from your Lord, O Muhammad, and a conquest and spoils, these people will say to you: Indeed, we were with you, meaning your brothers in religion, as God Almighty said: “Those who lie in wait for you - if you have a victory from God, they say, ‘We were not with you.’ But if the disbelievers have a share, they say, ‘Did we not gain control over you and protect you from the believers?’” And God Almighty said: Perhaps God will bring about victory or a decision from Him, and they will become, over what they concealed within themselves, regretful. And God Almighty said, informing about them here: And if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, ‘Indeed, we were with you.’ Then God Almighty said: Is not God most knowing of what is in the breasts of the worlds? That is, is God not most knowing of what is in their hearts and what their innermost thoughts conceal, even if they show you agreement. And the Almighty said: And that God will surely make evident those who have believed and He will surely make evident the hypocrites meaning that God will test people with hardship and ease, to distinguish these from those, those who obey God in hardship and ease, and those who obey Him only for their own gain, as God the Almighty said: And We will surely test you until We make evident those who strive among you [for the cause of God] and the steadfast, and We will make evident your report and the Almighty said after the Battle of Uhud, in which there was a test and examination: God would not leave the believers in that state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good Al-An’am 2:17.

29:12: God the Almighty says, informing us about the infidels of Quraysh, that they said to those among them who believed and followed the guidance: Return from your religion to our religion, and follow our path, and we will bear your sins, meaning and your sins, if you have sins in that, upon us and on our necks, as someone says: Do this and your sin is on my neck. God the Almighty said, refuting them: “And they will not bear any of their sins. Indeed, they are liars.” That is, in what they said, that they would bear the sins of those people, for no one bears the burden of another. God the Almighty says: And if a heavily laden animal calls for its load, nothing of it will be borne, even if he were a close relative. And God the Almighty says: “And no intimate friend will ask about an intimate friend. They will see them.” God the Almighty says: And they will bear their own burdens and other burdens besides their own, informing us about those who call to disbelief and misguidance, that on the Day of Resurrection they will bear their own burdens and the burdens of others because of the people they led astray, without that diminishing anything from their burdens, as God the Almighty says: They will bear their own burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection and also the burdens of those whom they led astray without knowledge, and in the Sahih: “Whoever calls to guidance will have a reward like the rewards of those who follow him until the Day of Resurrection, without that diminishing anything from their rewards. And whoever calls to misguidance will bear a sin like the sins of those who follow him until the Day of Resurrection, without that diminishing anything from their sins.” And in the Sahih: No soul is killed unjustly except that the first son of Adam will bear a share of its blood, because he was the first to institute killing. And the Almighty said: And they will be asked on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to invent, meaning they lied and fabricated slander. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned a hadith here and said: My father told us, Hisham bin Ammar told us, Sadaqah told us, Uthman bin Hafs bin Abi Al-Aliyah told us, Sulayman bin Habib Al-Maharibi told me on the authority of Abu Umamah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, conveyed what he was sent with, then he said: “Beware of injustice, for God will resolve on the Day of Resurrection and say: By My glory and majesty, injustice will not be permissible for me today. Then a caller will call out and say: Where is so-and-so, son of so-and-so? Then he will come, followed by good deeds like mountains, and people will stare at them until he stands before the Most Merciful, the Almighty. Then the caller will command and call out: Whoever has a claim or a wrong against so-and-so, son of so-and-so, come. So they will come until they gather and stand before the Most Merciful. Then the Most Merciful will say: Pay off My servant. They will say: How can we pay off his servant? He will say: Take for them from…” His good deeds, and they will continue to take from them until there is no good deed left, and there remain those who committed injustice. He will say: Pay off for My servant. They will say: He does not have a single good deed left. He will say: Take from their bad deeds and load them on him. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited this noble verse: And they will bear their burdens and other burdens with their burdens, and they will be asked on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to invent. This hadeeth has a corroborating report in Saheeh Abi Dawood from a different chain of narration: “A man will come on the Day of Resurrection with good deeds like mountains, but he wronged this one, took from the wealth of that one, and took from the honour of that one. So this one will take from his good deeds and this one from his good deeds. If he does not have a single good deed left, some of their bad deeds will be taken and thrown on him.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Abi Al-Hawari told us, Abu Bishr Al-Hadha’ told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza Al-Thamali, on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: “O Muadh, the believer will be asked on the Day of Resurrection about all his efforts, even about the kohl applied to his eyes and about the crumbs of clay on two fingers. So do not let me find you coming on the Day of Resurrection and no one happier with what God has given you than you.”

29:16: God Almighty tells us about His servant, messenger, and friend, Abraham, the leader of the monotheists, that he called his people to worship God alone, with no partner, and to be sincere to Him in piety, and to seek provision from Him alone, with no partner, and to make Him one in gratitude, for He is the One to whom thanks are due for blessings, and no one else gives them. That is better for you, if you only knew, meaning, if you do that, good will come to you in this world and the next, and evil will be warded off from you in this world and the next. Then God Almighty informed us that the idols they worship do not harm or benefit, and you only invented names for them and called them gods, but they are created like you. This is how Al-Awfi narrated it from Ibn Abbas, and Mujahid and Al-Suddi said the same. Al-Walibi narrated from Ibn Abbas: And you fabricate falsehood, meaning, you carve them into idols. Mujahid said the same in one narration, as did Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others, and it was chosen by him. Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him. And it does not possess for you provision. So seek provision from God. This is more expressive in restriction, like His saying: You alone do we worship, and You alone do we ask for help. “My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise.” For this reason, He said: So seek meaning, ask from God provision, meaning not from anyone else, because no one else possesses anything. What is apparent from the context is that all of this is from the words of Abraham, peace be upon him, as evidence against them to prove the Resurrection, because he said after all of this: {And what was the answer of his people?} And God knows best.

29:19: God Almighty says, informing us about Abraham, peace be upon him, that he guided them to prove the resurrection which they deny, based on what they witness in themselves of God’s creation of them after they were nothing worth mentioning, then they found and became hearing and seeing people. He who began this is able to restore it, for it is easy for Him and simple for Him. Then He guided them to consider what is in the horizons of the observable signs of God’s creation of things: the heavens and what is in them of luminous fixed and moving planets, the earths and what is in them of cradles and mountains, valleys and wildernesses and deserts, trees and rivers, fruits and seas. All of that indicates their occurrence in themselves, and the existence of their Creator, the Doer and Chooser, who says to the thing, Be, and it is. For this reason, He said: Have they not seen how God originates creation and then repeats it? Indeed, that, for God, is easy. Like His Almighty saying: And it is He who originates creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him. Then God Almighty said: “Say, ‘Travel through the earth and observe how He originated creation. Then God will produce the final creation.’” On the Day of Resurrection, ‘Indeed, God is over all things competent.’ This position is similar to the Almighty’s saying: We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. And like the Almighty’s saying: Or were they created by nothing, or were they the creators? Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they are not certain. And the Almighty’s saying: He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills means that He is the ruling judge who does what He wills and rules as He wants. There is no one to question His ruling, and He is not questioned about what He does, while they will be questioned. He has the creation and the command, and whatever He does, He is just, because He is the Owner who does not wrong by the weight of an atom, as came in the hadith narrated by the people of the Sunnah: If God were to punish the inhabitants of His heavens and the inhabitants of His earth, He would punish them, and He is not unjust to them. For this reason, the Almighty said: He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned meaning you will be returned on the Day of Resurrection. And the Almighty says: And you will not escape [God] on earth or in heaven. That is, none of the inhabitants of His heavens or earth can escape Him. Rather, He is the Supreme over His servants, so everything that fears Him is in need of Him, and He is independent of anything other than Him. “And you have not besides God any protector or helper. And those who disbelieve in the signs of God and in the meeting with Him” that is, they deny them and disbelieve in the Hereafter. Those have despaired of My mercy. That is, they have no share in it. And those will have a painful punishment. That is, a severe, painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter.

I went to him and a man came and the people separated, and he was wearing a cloak. It was Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas. When Nawf saw him, he stopped talking. Only the worst of its people will remain on the earth. Their land will spit them out, and the soul of the Most Merciful will detest them. The Fire will gather them with the monkeys and pigs, and it will spend the night with them when they spend the night, and it will take a nap with them when they nap, and it will eat whoever of them stayed behind.” He said: And I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “People of my nation will emerge from the east who will recite the Qur’an, but it will not go beyond their collarbones. Whenever a group of them emerges, it will cut off…” “Whenever a generation of them emerges, it will be cut off - until he counted it more than twenty times - whenever a generation of them emerges, it will be cut off until the Dajjal emerges among the rest of them.” Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Abu Dawud and Abd al-Samad, both of them on the authority of Hisham al-Dastawai on the authority of Qatada. Then I saw us in the end now, and the dinar and dirham were dearer to each of us than his Muslim brother. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “If you follow the tails of cows, and engage in `inah transactions, and abandon jihad in the way of God, God will impose humiliation on your necks that will not be removed from you until you return to what you were upon and repent to God Almighty.” And I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There will be migration after migration to the migration of your father Abraham until there remains on the earth only the worst of its people, and their land will spit them out, and the spirit of the Most Merciful will detest them, and the Fire will gather them with the monkeys and pigs, taking a nap with them when they nap, and spending the night with them where they spend the night, and whatever falls from them will be for it.” And I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “A people will emerge From my nation, there are those who do evil deeds. They recite the Qur’an, but it does not go beyond their throats. Yazid said: I do not know of anyone who did not say that. One of you would consider his knowledge insignificant compared to their knowledge. They kill the people of Islam. Whenever they revolt, kill them. Whenever they revolt, kill them. Whenever they revolt, kill them. Whenever they revolt, kill them. Whenever a group of them rises, God kills them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, repeated that twenty times or more, and I was listening. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Al-Hasan bin Al-Fadl told us, Abdullah bin Jaafar told us, Yaqoub bin Sufyan told us, Abu Al-Nadr Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Yazid and Hisham bin Ammar Al-Dimashqi told us: Yahya bin Hamza told us, Al-Awza’i told us, on the authority of Nafi’, and Abu Al-Nadr said, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The people of the Earth will migrate, migration after migration, to the place of migration of Abraham, until none remains but the wickedest of its people. It will spend the night with them wherever they spend the night, and it will take with it whatever they have lost.” This is strange from the hadith of Nafi’, and it appears that Al-Awza’i narrated it from a sheikh of his who was among the weak, and God knows best. His narration from the hadith of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas is closer to memory. And the Almighty’s saying: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob is like His saying: So when he had left them and what they worshipped besides God, We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and each of them We made a prophet meaning that when he left his people, God comforted his eyes with the presence of a righteous son, a prophet, and a righteous son, a prophet, was born to him during his grandfather’s lifetime. Similarly, God the Almighty said: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional meaning an addition, as God the Almighty said: So We gave her good tidings of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob meaning that a son would be born to this son during your lifetimes, who would comfort your eyes. And the fact that Jacob was a son to Isaac is stated in the Qur’an and confirmed by the Prophetic Sunnah. God the Almighty said: “Or were you witnesses when death approached Jacob, when he said to his sons, ‘What will you worship after me?’ They said, ‘We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac - one God’” (10:14). And the Almighty’s saying: And We placed among his descendants prophethood and the Book. This is a great and noble garment, along with God’s choosing him as a friend, and making him an imam for the people, by placing prophethood and the Book among his descendants. All the prophets of the Children of Israel were from the lineage of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, until the last of them was Jesus, son of Mary. He rose among their people, giving good tidings of the Arab Qurayshi Hashemite Prophet, the Seal of the Messengers, and the Master of the children of Adam in this world and the Hereafter, whom God chose from the heart of the pure Arabs, from the lineage of Ishmael, son of Abraham, peace be upon them both. And His statement: And We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter, he will be among the righteous. For this reason, God Almighty said: And We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter, he will be among the righteous. 29:31: When Lot, peace be upon him, sought help from God Almighty against them, God sent angels to help him. They passed by Abraham, peace be upon him, in the form of guests. He brought them what a guest should have. When he saw that they had no interest in food, he disliked them and was afraid of them. When the good report came to Abraham and they told him that they had been sent to destroy the people of Lot, he began to defend himself, hoping that God would guide them. And when they said, Indeed, we will destroy the people of this city, he said, Indeed, Lot is among them. They said, “We know best who is in it. We will surely save him and his family, except for his wife; she was among those who remained behind,” meaning among those who were destroyed, because she had been collaborating with them in their disbelief, transgression, and plotting. Then they left him and entered upon Lot in the form of handsome young men. When he saw them like that, bad. “And he was distressed by their situation.” That is, he was distressed by their situation. Indeed, We are going to send down upon the people of this city a punishment from the sky because they used to commit wickedness.’” That is because Gabriel, peace be upon him, uprooted their city from the depths of the earth, then raised it to the clouds of heaven, then turned it upside down on them. God sent upon them stones of layered baked clay, marked with your Lord, and they are not far from the wrongdoers. God made in their place a foul, stinking lake, and made them a lesson until the Day of Calling. They are among the most severely punished people on the Day of Resurrection. For this reason, God Almighty said, And We have certainly left of it a clear sign, that is, clear for a people who understand, just as God Almighty said, “And indeed, you pass by them in the morning and by night. This was because they were reducing the measures and weights and blocking the way for people. This was in addition to their disbelief in God and His Messenger. So God destroyed them with a great earthquake that shook their land, and a shout that tore hearts from their throats, and the punishment of the Day of Shadow that snatched souls from their homes. Qatada said: Dead. Another said: Some of them had been thrown on top of others.

29:38: God Almighty tells us about these nations who denied the Messengers, how He annihilated them and diversified their punishment, and took revenge on them. The people of Hud, peace be upon him, lived in Al-Ahqaf, which is close to Hadramaut in Yemen. The people of Thamud, the people of Salih, lived in Al-Hijr, close to Wadi Al-Qura. The Arabs knew their dwellings well and passed by them often. There was Qarun, the owner of abundant wealth and the keys to heavy treasures. Pharaoh, the king of Egypt in the time of Moses, and his minister Haman, the Copts who disbelieved in God Almighty and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, So We seized each one for his sin, meaning his punishment was appropriate for him. And among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones, and they were the people of Aad. This was because they said: Who is stronger than us? Then a fierce, cold wind came upon them, blowing very violently, carrying gravel from the earth and throwing it upon them, uprooting them from the earth, raising a man from the earth to the height of the sky, then turning him back on his head and smashing him, so that he remained a body without a head, as if they were trunks of hollowed-out palm trees. And among them were those whom the blast seized - they were Thamud. The proof was established against them and the evidence was made clear to them from that she-camel from which the rock split, just as they had asked him, and despite this they did not believe, but rather continued in their transgression and disbelief, and threatened the Prophet of God, Salih, and those who believed with him, and promised them that they would expel them and stone them. Then a blast came upon them that silenced their voices and movements. And among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow - they were Qarun, who transgressed, transgressed, and rebelled, and disobeyed the Most High Lord, and walked on the earth exultantly, and rejoiced and wasted himself, and believed that he was better than others, and strutted in his gait, so God caused the earth to swallow him and his home. The earth, and he will continue to sink into it until the Day of Resurrection. And among them were those We drowned, namely Pharaoh, his minister Haman, and their entire army. They were drowned in a single morning, so none of them escaped. And God would not have wronged them, that is, in what He did to them, but they were wronging themselves. That is, He only did that to them as a recompense for what their hands had earned. What we have mentioned is the apparent context of the verse, which is a case of twisting and spreading, which is that He mentioned the nations who denied, then He said, So each We seized for his sin, that is, of those mentioned. I only drew attention to this because Ibn Jurayj narrated that Ibn Abbas said, in His statement, And among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones, that is, the people of Lot. And among them were those We drowned, that is, the people of Noah. This is disconnected from Ibn Abbas, as Ibn Jurayj did not meet him. Then God mentioned in this Surah the destruction of the people of Noah by the flood, and the people of Lot by the sending down of punishment from the sky, and He prolonged the context and the separation between that and this context. Qatada said, And among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones, meaning the people of Lot, and among them were those whom the blast seized, meaning the people of Shu’ayb. This is also far-fetched for what came before, and God knows best.

29:44: God the Almighty says, informing us of His great power that He created the heavens and the earth in truth, meaning not in vain or playful ways, That every soul may be recompensed for what it strives for, “That He may recompense those who do evil for what they have done and recompense those who do good with good.” And His statement, Indeed in that is a sign for the believers, meaning a clear indication that He the Almighty is the One who is unique in creation, management, and divinity. Then God the Almighty says, commanding His Messenger and the believers to recite the Qur’an, which is to recite it and convey it to the people, “And establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of God is greater.” Meaning that prayer includes two things: abandoning immorality and wrongdoing, meaning that being consistent in it motivates one to abandon them. It was stated in the hadith narrated by Imran and Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, Whoever’s prayer does not prevent him from immorality and wrongdoing, it only increases his distance from God. Mention the effects mentioned in this regard Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Mukharami al-Fallas narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Nafi’ Abu Ziyad narrated to us, Umar ibn Abi Uthman narrated to us, al-Hasan narrated to us, on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the statement of God, Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing. He said: Whoever’s prayer does not prohibit immorality and wrongdoing, then there is no prayer for him. Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Talhah al-Yarbu’i narrated to us, Abu Mu’awiyah narrated to us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever’s prayer does not prohibit immorality and wrongdoing, then it only increases his distance from God. At-Tabarani narrated it from the hadith of Abu Mu’awiyah. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Khalid bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Al-Ala bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of someone who mentioned it, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God, Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, he said: So whoever’s prayer does not enjoin good and prohibits evil, his prayer only increases him in distance from God. This is a suspended narration. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Ali bin Hashim bin Al-Barid told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said: There is no prayer for the one who does not obey prayer, and obeying prayer is that it prohibits immorality and wrongdoing. Sufyan said, They said, O Shu’aib, your prayer commands you. Sufyan said: Yes, by God, it commands him and prohibits him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj narrated to us, Abu Khalid narrated to us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said - and Abu Khalid said once on the authority of Abdullah -: There is no prayer for the one who does not obey the prayer, and obeying the prayer prevents him from indecency and wrongdoing. The suspended narration is more authentic, as Al-A’mash narrated on the authority of Malik bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Yazid, who said: It was said to Abdullah: So-and-so prolongs his prayer. He said: Prayer is of no benefit except to the one who obeys it. Ibn Jarir said: Ali narrated to us, Ismail bin Muslim narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever performs a prayer that does not prevent him from indecency and wrongdoing, will only increase his distance from God because of it. The most authentic in all of this are the suspended narrations from Ibn Mas’ud, Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-A’mash and others, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Yusuf ibn Musa told us, Jarir - meaning Ibn Abd al-Hamid - told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, who said: I think it was on the authority of Jabir - al-A’mash was uncertain - who said: “A man said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: So-and-so prays at night, but when morning comes, he steals.” He said: What you say will stop him. Muhammad ibn Musa al-Jurashi told us, Ziyad ibn Abdullah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, something similar, and he did not have any doubts. Then he said: This hadith has been narrated on the authority of al-A’mash by more than one person, and they differed in its chain of narration. More than one person narrated it on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, or someone else. Qais said, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir. Jarir and Ziyad said, on the authority of Abdullah, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Jabir. Imam Ahmad said: Wakee' narrated to us, Al-A'mash narrated to us, Abu Salih narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: "A man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: 'So-and-so prays at night, but in the morning he steals.' The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: 'What you say will stop him.'" Prayer also includes remembrance of God, which is the greatest requirement. For this reason, God the Almighty said: And the remembrance of God is greater, meaning greater than the first, and God knows that which you do, meaning He knows all your deeds and words. Abu Al-Aaliyah said about the verse: Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, that prayer has three characteristics, so any prayer that does not have any of these characteristics is not prayer: sincerity, fear of God, and remembrance of God. Sincerity commands one to do what is right, fear of God forbids what is wrong, and remembrance of God and the Qur'an commands and forbids what is wrong. Ibn 'Awn Al-Ansari said: When you are praying, then you are doing what is right, and it has kept you away from immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of God that you are doing is greater. Hammad ibn Abi Sulaiman said, Prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, meaning as long as you are performing it. Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, And the remembrance of God is greater, meaning: And the remembrance of God of His servants is greater when they remember Him than their remembering Him. This is what was narrated by more than one person on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Mujahid and others said the same. Ibn Abi Hatim said, Abu Saeed al-Ashj told us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “And the remembrance of God is greater, meaning: The remembrance of God when you eat and when you sleep. I said, A companion of mine at home says something other than what you say. He said, What does he say? I said, God says, ‘Remember Me; I will remember you.’ So the remembrance of God of us is greater than our remembrance of Him. He said, He is truthful. He said, “My father told us, al-Nufaili told us, Ismail told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, “And the remembrance of God is greater,” he said, “It has two aspects. He said, The remembrance of God when He forbade it.” He said, And the remembrance of God of you is greater than your remembrance of Him. Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, Hisham told us, Ata ibn as-Sa’ib told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Rabi’ah, who said: Ibn Abbas said to me: Do you know what is meant by the words of God the Almighty: And the remembrance of God is greater? I said: Yes. He said: What is it? I said: Tasbeeh, tahmeed, and takbeer in prayer, reciting the Quran, and the like. He said: You have said something strange, but it is not like that. Rather, he only says: God’s remembrance of you when He has commanded or forbidden something, if you remember Him, it is greater than your remembrance of Him. This has been narrated from Ibn Abbas through other chains of narration. It has also been narrated from Ibn Mas’ud, Abu al-Darda’, Salman al-Farisi, and others, and Ibn Jarir chose it.

29:46: Qatada and others said: This verse was abrogated by the verse of the sword, and there is no longer any argument with them, rather it is Islam, the jizyah, or the sword. Others said: Rather, it remains and is decisive for whoever among them wants insight into the religion, so he argues in the best way to be more effective in it, as God the Almighty said: Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction (al-Baqarah 2:17), and God the Almighty said to Moses and Aaron when He sent them to Pharaoh: And speak to him with gentle speech that perhaps he may be reminded or fear (al-Baqarah 2:17). This statement was chosen by Ibn Jarir, who narrated it from Ibn Zayd. And the Almighty said: Except those among them who have wronged meaning they have deviated from the path of truth, and have been blind to the clear path, and have been stubborn and obstinate. Then the argument moves to the battle, and they fight with what prevents and deters them. God the Almighty said: “Indeed, We sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Scripture and the balance that people may maintain justice. And We sent down iron, wherein is great force and benefits for people, so that God may make evident who supports Him and His messengers unseen. Indeed, God is Powerful and Exalted in Might.” Jabir said: We ordered whoever disobeyed the Book of God to strike him with the sword. Mujahid said: Except those among them who have wronged meaning the people of war, and whoever among them refused to pay the jizyah. And the Almighty’s saying: And say, ‘We believe in that which was revealed to us and revealed to you,’ meaning if they tell us something whose truth or falsehood we do not know, then we do not deny it because it may be true, nor do we believe it because it may be false. Rather, we believe in it with a general belief, conditional upon a condition, which is that it is revealed and not changed or interpreted. Al-Bukhari may God have mercy on him said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Uthman ibn Umar told us, Ali ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, who said: The People of the Book used to recite the Torah in Hebrew and explain it in Arabic for the Muslims. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “Do not believe the People of the Book and do not disbelieve them, but say: We believe in God and in what was revealed to us and what was revealed to you. Our God and your God is one, and we are Muslims in submission to Him.” This hadith is unique to Al-Bukhari. Imam Ahmad said: Uthman ibn Amr told us, Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Ibn Abi Namlah told me that Abu Namlah Al-Ansari told him that while he was sitting with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), a Jewish man came to him and said: O Muhammad, does this funeral procession speak? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: God knows best. The Jew said: I testify that it speaks. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: When the People of the Book speak to you, do not believe them or disbelieve them, but say: We believe in God, His Books, and His Messengers. If it is true, then you will not disbelieve them, and if it is false, then you will not believe them. I said This Abu Namlah is Ammarah. It was also said that he is Ammar, and it was also said that he is Amr ibn Muadh ibn Zararah Al-Ansari may God be pleased with him. Then it should be known that most of what they speak of is mostly lies and slander, because it has been distorted, altered, changed, and interpreted. How little truth there is in it, and how little benefit there is in much of it if it were true. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Abu Asim told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Amir, on the authority of Ammarah ibn Umair, on the authority of Harith ibn Zuhair, on the authority of Ubaydullah - he is Ibn Mas`ud - who said: Do not ask the People of the Book about anything, for they will never guide you, and they have gone astray. Either you deny the truth or believe in falsehood, for there is no one among the People of the Book who does not have in his heart a desire calling him to his religion, like the desire for money. Al-Bukhari said: Musa ibn Isma`il told us, Ibrahim ibn Sa`d told us, Ibn Shihab told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: How can you ask the People of the Book about anything, while your Book, which was revealed to you through the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), is the most recent. You recite it pure and unalloyed. And it has told you that the People of the Book altered and changed it and wrote the Book with their own hands and said, It is from God, in order to exchange it for a small price. Doesn’t the knowledge that has come to you forbid you from asking them? No, by God, we have never seen a man among them ask you about that which has been revealed to you. Al-Bukhari said: Abu Al-Yaman said: Shuaib told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Humaid bin Abd Al-Rahman told me that he heard Muawiyah speaking to a group of Quraysh in Madinah, and he mentioned Ka’b Al-Ahbar, and he said: He is one of the most truthful of these narrators of hadith who narrate from the People of the Book, and we still test him for lying. I said The meaning is that he lies linguistically, unintentionally, because he narrates from scriptures that he thinks well of, and in them are fabricated and false things, because there were no memorizers in their religion who were as skilled as this great nation. Despite that, and in recent times, many hadiths have been fabricated in this nation, and no one knows them except God, the Almighty, and whoever God has granted knowledge of that, each one according to his ability, and to God be praise and thanks.
29:47: Ibn Jarir said: God the Almighty says, Just as We sent down the Book to the Messengers before you, O Muhammad, thus We sent down this Book to you. What he said is good, and its relevance and connection are good. And God Almighty says: Then do they believe in falsehood and deny the favor of God? That is, was their gratitude for this great favor by associating partners with Him and worshipping other idols and rivals with Him, and exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and caused their people to dwell in the home of ruin and disbelieved in God’s Prophet, servant, and Messenger? So it was appropriate for them to sincerely worship God, not to associate partners with Him, and to believe in the Messenger, glorify him, and honor him. But they denied him and fought him, and expelled him from among them. For this reason, God Almighty took away from them what was bestowed upon them. He attacked them and killed those of them who were killed at Badr. Then the state became for God, His Messenger, and the believers. So God opened Mecca to His Messenger, and humiliated their noses and humiliated their necks. Then God the Almighty said: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about God or denies the truth when it has come to him? That is, no one is more severely punished than one who lies about God and says: God revealed to him, while nothing has been revealed to him. And whoever says: I will reveal the like of what God revealed, and so on, no one is more severely punished than one who denies the truth when it has come to him. The first is a slanderer and the second is a liar. That is why God the Almighty said: Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers? Then God the Almighty said: And those who strive for Us, meaning the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, his companions and his followers until the Day of Judgment. We will surely guide them to Our ways, that is, We will surely show them Our ways, meaning Our paths in this world and the hereafter. And indeed, God is with the doers of good} He said: Those who do what they know, God will guide them to what they do not know. Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari said: So I told it to Abu Sulayman al-Darani, and he liked it and said: It is not appropriate for one who is inspired to do something good to do it until he hears it in a tradition. So when he hears it in a tradition, he acts upon it and praises God until it agrees with what is in his heart. And His statement, {And indeed, God is with the doers of good} Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Isa ibn Ja'far, the judge of Rayy, told us, Abu Ja'far al-Razi told us, on the authority of al-Mughirah, on the authority of al-Sha'bi, who said: Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, said: “Indeed, goodness is only to do good to those who wrong you. Goodness is not to do good to those who do good to you.” And God knows best. End of the interpretation of Surat al-'Ankaboot. All praise and thanks are due to God.

That is, was their gratitude for this great favor by associating partners with Him and worshipping other idols and rivals with Him, and exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and caused their people to dwell in the home of ruin and disbelieved in God’s Prophet, servant, and Messenger? So it was appropriate for them to sincerely worship God, not to associate partners with Him, and to believe in the Messenger, glorify him, and honor him. But they denied him and fought him, and expelled him from among them. For this reason, God Almighty took away from them what was bestowed upon them. He attacked them and killed those of them who were killed at Badr. Then the state became for God, His Messenger, and the believers. So God opened Mecca to His Messenger, and humiliated their noses and humiliated their necks. Then God the Almighty said: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about God or denies the truth when it has come to him? That is, no one is more severely punished than one who lies about God and says: God revealed to him, while nothing has been revealed to him. And whoever says: I will reveal the like of what God revealed, and so on, no one is more severely punished than one who denies the truth when it has come to him. The first is a slanderer and the second is a liar. That is why God the Almighty said: Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers? Then God the Almighty said: And those who strive for Us, meaning the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, his companions and his followers until the Day of Judgment. We will surely guide them to Our ways, that is, We will surely show them Our ways, meaning Our paths in this world and the hereafter. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari told us, Abbas al-Hamdani Abu Ahmad from the people of Acre told us regarding the statement of God the Most High: {And those who strive for Us - We will surely guide them to Our ways. And indeed, God is with the doers of good} He said: Those who do what they know, God will guide them to what they do not know. Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari said: So I told it to Abu Sulayman al-Darani, and he liked it and said: It is not appropriate for one who is inspired to do something good to do it until he hears it in a tradition. So when he hears it in a tradition, he acts upon it and praises God until it agrees with what is in his heart. And His statement, {And indeed, God is with the doers of good} Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Isa ibn Ja'far, the judge of Rayy, told us, Abu Ja'far al-Razi told us, on the authority of al-Mughirah, on the authority of al-Sha'bi, who said: Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, said: “Indeed, goodness is only to do good to those who wrong you. Goodness is not to do good to those who do good to you.” And God knows best. End of the interpretation of Surat al-'Ankaboot. All praise and thanks are due to God.
